narrative.human_title: Lugia at the Team GR doorway
narrative.why_it_matters: This Lugia feels like a sequel object in the best way. Dragonite gave the first Card GB a legendary myth inside the cartridge; GB2 gives Lugia a darker stage, paired with Team GR's Mewtwo and a game that stayed in Japan. The result is a card with a tiny GB symbol doing a lot of work: it marks software, villain-story, Gen II myth, and late-WotC promo memory all at once. That is why the assembly matters more than the name alone.

narrative.human_title: Lugia with the sequel's GB mark
narrative.why_it_matters: Lugia already carries storm and ocean myth, but this print gives it a stranger job: it helps a Japan-only Game Boy sequel leave a cardboard trace. The GB symbol is small, almost modest, and yet it tells the whole story if an agent knows how to read it. This is not Neo Genesis thunder and not a movie pamphlet echo. It is Lugia as a software insert, paired against Team GR's Mewtwo, right where Pokemon was learning to let cards, games, villains, and collecting rituals talk to each other.
